---
title: "Do the numbers agree? A data audit of the 2025-26 Atlantic 10 season"
author: "Ian Kachadorian"
output:
  html_document:
    theme: flatly
    toc: false
    self_contained: true
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 3.6, dpi = 144)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
a <- readRDS("output/audit.rds")
d <- a$discrepancies
cs <- a$check_summary
ss <- a$stat_summary
gs <- a$game_summary
n <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",")
pct <- function(x, digits = 1) paste0(formatC(100 * x, format = "f", digits = digits), "%")
team_chk <- cs[cs$check == "Play-by-play vs team box", ]
ast <- ss[ss$stat == "Assists", ]
rest <- ss[ss$stat != "Assists", ]
worst <- gs[1, ]
host <- a$assist_by_host
tm <- a$assist_by_team
bona <- tm[tm$team == "St. Bonaventure", ]
ooo <- sum(a$integrity$out_of_order > 0)
accent <- "#1f5f8b"
```

**The question.** Every game produces three records of the same events: the play-by-play log, the team box score and the player box score. If the data is right, all three agree. I pulled the public ESPN data for every game an Atlantic 10 team played in 2025-26 (`r n(nrow(a$games))` games, `r n(sum(gs$events))` play-by-play events) and counted each one against the others, the same way a stock count is reconciled against the ledger.

**The answer.** The data is good but not clean. Of `r n(sum(cs$comparisons))` comparisons, `r n(nrow(d))` disagree, and `r n(sum(gs$clean))` of `r n(nrow(gs))` games reconcile completely. Scoring is exact: points, made threes and made free throws match in every team-game. The errors sit in the judgment stats, and one stat, assists, accounts for `r pct(mean(d$stat == "Assists"), 0)` of them.

## What I found

1. **Assists are the weak point.** Play-by-play assists match the team box score in only `r pct(ast$match_rate)` of team-games; every other stat matches in `r pct(min(rest$match_rate))` or more. The play-by-play is short by a net `r n(ast$box_total - ast$pbp_total)` assists over the season.

2. **The assist gap depends on where the game was played.** In games hosted by `r host$host[1]`, `r pct(host$share_off[1], 0)` of team-games have an assist mismatch. In games hosted by `r host$host[nrow(host)]`, it is `r pct(host$share_off[nrow(host)], 0)`. That points to how each arena's scoring crew enters assists, not to random error. I have not confirmed the cause; the pattern is what the data shows.

3. **It changes a ranking.** By the box score, St. Bonaventure was `r bona$rank_box`nd in the conference in assists per game (`r formatC(bona$box_per_game, format = "f", digits = 1)`). Counted from play-by-play, they drop to `r bona$rank_pbp`th (`r formatC(bona$pbp_per_game, format = "f", digits = 1)`). Any lineup or on/off assist number built from play-by-play carries that error.

4. **One game holds `r pct(worst$mismatches / nrow(d), 0)` of all mismatches.** `r worst$matchup` (`r worst$game_date`) has `r worst$mismatches` on its own: missing three-point attempts, turnovers, steals and fouls for both teams, which looks like a stretch of the game missing from the feed.

5. **The obvious sort key is wrong.** Sorting events by `sequence_number` puts them out of game order in `r n(ooo)` of `r n(nrow(gs))` games (`r n(sum(a$integrity$out_of_order))` places where the clock runs backward). Sorting by `game_play_number` is correct in every game. Anyone computing lineups or runs from the wrong column gets wrong answers without an error message.

```{r stat-chart}
ss |>
  mutate(stat = reorder(stat, -match_rate), flag = stat == "Assists") |>
  ggplot(aes(match_rate, stat, fill = flag)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = pct(match_rate)), hjust = -0.15, size = 3.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#c8553d", `FALSE` = accent), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1.08), breaks = seq(0, 1, .25)) +
  labs(title = "Share of team-games where play-by-play matches the box score", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), plot.title.position = "plot")
```

```{r host-chart}
host |>
  mutate(host = reorder(host, share_off)) |>
  ggplot(aes(share_off, host)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, fill = accent) +
  geom_text(aes(label = pct(share_off, 0)), hjust = -0.15, size = 3.2) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, max(host$share_off) * 1.15)) +
  labs(title = "Share of team-games with an assist mismatch, by host arena", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), plot.title.position = "plot")
```

## The checks

```{r check-table}
cs |>
  transmute(
    Check = check, Comparisons = n(comparisons), Mismatches = n(mismatches),
    `Match rate` = pct(match_rate, 2), `Games affected` = games_affected
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lrrrr")
```

- **Play-by-play vs team box:** 14 stats per team per game, counted from events and compared with the official team line.
- **Play-by-play vs player box:** the same stats for each player.
- **Player box sum vs team box:** the player lines must add up to the team line.
- **Player minutes vs game length:** 200 team minutes, plus 25 for each overtime.
- **Box score arithmetic:** points equal twos, threes and free throws; total rebounds equal offensive plus defensive; each team's opponent score equals the opponent's own score.

## Limits

This is public ESPN data loaded with the `hoopR` package, not CBB Analytics' own feed, so the specific errors may differ from yours. The scores in this play-by-play were rebuilt by `hoopR`, so the running score cannot be tested independently. A mismatch shows that two records disagree; it does not show which one is right. That takes film or the official scorer's report.

The method carries over to any feed. Every mismatch is listed by game, team and player in `output/discrepancies.csv` and in the app (`app.R`).
